name: DUMAND
full_name: Deep Underwater Muon and Neutrino Detector
summary: A pioneering Hawaii-based project developed deep-ocean neutrino-telescope technology but ended before the planned complete array could operate.
detection_principle: Underwater optical modules were intended to reconstruct Cherenkov light from muons produced near a deep-sea array. A short prototype string measured cosmic-ray muons and a later shore-cabled deployment tested full-depth infrastructure.

sites.name: DUMAND offshore site
sites.location: Pacific Ocean west of Keahole Point, Hawaii

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The University of Hawaii explicitly dates the programme to approximately 1976–1995 and describes cancellation.

timeline.event: International design workshops initiated the programme.
Short prototype string demonstrated underwater muon measurements.
First full-depth shore-cabled string deployed, then affected by electrical faults.
US Department of Energy cancelled further support.

collaboration.name: DUMAND Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Planned depth
key_parameters.value: Approximately 4,800 m offshore Keahole Point, Hawaii

key_parameters.name: Implemented hardware
key_parameters.value: Short prototype string; one full-depth string plus junction box and shore cable in 1993

results.summary: Developed ocean-optics, optical-module and cabling techniques that influenced later water and ice telescopes; the complete planned neutrino observatory was never realised.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.

media.caption: Early DUMAND cubic-kilometre concept and the smaller nine-string DUMAND-II design; neither full array was completed.
